questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I'm also a British citizen so that was definitely a deciding factor in choosing the UK.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy! The host university was super helpful. There was a reception open 24/7 and other students that really helped you out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to have some help with the heating in my room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You were offered a room which I decided to do. It was on the expensive side, but I have no regrets. It was so nice to be so close to classes and that the quality was guaranteed through the university.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a shared kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There's apparently quite the difference between the different buildings. Mine was completely newly renovated and very nice. However, this isn't necessarily a given.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Course registration happens significantly later than at home but it was super easy and convenient.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I emailed with one of the course coordinators who helped signed me up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Lots of help for so many different things. It's difficult to list.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely successful - I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much? It was very easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was overall very good, but just a different way of being taught compared to at home. You're a very small group of students for seminars.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally a very high level of courses. Reading was perhaps a little lighter than at UCPH. Professors very good. The expectations for active participation are different and higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More intimate (we were never more than 20 people for a class and sometimes only 3 students for seminars).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Governance
Morality and Modern Warfare
Elections and Voting Behaviour

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the two latter courses I listed, but the first wasn't my favourite.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Added costs of getting everything home at the end. I had more weight than anticipated and had to pay extra to check more luggage.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was definitely more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many different societies and events - there's really nothing like this at UCPH, sadly.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Loads of different sports, fitness, societies (book clubs, music groups etc.)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a couple societies to meet other people, join some of the bus tours for international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore York! It's such a lovely city, make sure you see it all. So many sights and some amazing places to eat and drink. Definitely also recommend seeing some of the nearby towns.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I personally found it very easy but am also a British citizen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I honestly didn't socialise much with local students. Our housing was only for visiting students so I mainly spent time with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Small things like being more open to strangers? We're generally more private in Denmark, but in York you'd joke more with people you don't know. Always say hi and bye to the bus drivers etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and kindness among people. The sights.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Explore the city and nearby cities,
Join a few societies,
Spend time with fellow students

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing that hasn't been mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just the overall experiences you gain from living in a completely different city? It's incredibly rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I guess being far away from family during special occasions or when things get tough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Highly recommend York!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
